thread:
Clara: Heads-up — seeing a sharp uptick in preemptive evictions and Pending tiny-gpu pods in eu-west1c since ~09:12 UTC. Node warmpool attach failures + a bunch of small jobs stuck.
Nate: Ok, is this across racks or concentrated to a few AZ hosts?
Clara: Mostly eu-west1c rack-11 and rack-12. Scheduler logs show fence/attach timeouts and a backlog on warmpool attach.
Ajay: Screenshot of scheduler metric: preemptions/sec jumped x8 at 09:12. Also, tail of kube-scheduler shows repeated "failed to admit pod: node(s) had taints" then quick preempt.
Mika: Any recent label/taint rollout? We pushed the new anti-affinity strictness yesterday night.
Clara: Yep — the affinity rollout v2 landed 03:00 UTC. My hunch: stricter anti-affinity + smaller warm pool in eu-west1c => fragmentation and more tiny pods forced to preempt.
Nate: That matches cost telemetry — tokenized jobs spilled to on-demand high-mem instances earlier, cost spike seen in infra-costs dashboard.
Ajay: Quick mitigation options: relax anti-affinity for tiny-gpu class, increase warmpool size temporarily, or allow soft-affinity fallback. Which is safest short-term?
Mika: Prefer warmpool bump + soft-affinity fallback. Relaxing affinity globally could introduce noisy neighbor regressions.
Clara: I can roll a hotfix to scheduler config to enable softAffinityFallback for nodeSelector "resource.gpu:size=tiny" in eu-west1c only. Patch plan:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: scheduler-config
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  policies: |
    - name: tiny-gpu-soft-fallback
      selectors:
        - matchExpressions:
            - {key: "resource.gpu:size", operator: In, values: ["tiny"]}
      action: soft-affinity-fallback
EOF
```
Clara: Also will scale warmpool: `warmpoolctl scale --region eu-west1c --pool tiny-gpu --delta +20`
Nate: Sounds good. Ops-bot, can you run a quick pre-check for any running rollout that would conflict? @ops-bot
ops-bot: running preflight checks...
ops-bot: preflight: no concurrent scheduler-config rollouts, warmpool quota available (can add +20 without hitting quota), api latency within normal.
Ajay: After hotfix we should monitor: scheduler admit latency, evictions/sec, pending count, and cost shift (ensure not spilling into bigger instance types). Suggest 15 min check, then 1h.
Mika: Also add a short-lived canary: target 25% of tiny-gpu pods to use soft-fallback first, then flip to 100% if stable.
Clara: Rolling the config now to eu-west1c canary (10%): applying config and scaling warmpool +10 first. I'll post status in 5m.
Nate: If we still see high conntrack/attach errors maybe network path to warp attachment service is flaking — watch attach error logs `attach-service` -> `ECONNRESET` / `context deadline exceeded`.
Clara: Noted. If that happens we'll divert attach traffic to eu-west1b as fallback.
Ajay: Filing a short incident ticket and tagging oncall: ENG-PLAT-1234. Add action items and rollback plan.
Clara: Ticket created ENG-PLAT-1234.rolling: hotfix -> canary -> scale -> monitor. Will update thread. :thumbsup:
Mika: Thanks. If canary looks good let's keep soft-fallback for 4h then evaluate with packing/eviction metrics and cost.
Clara: Update 5m: canary applied, warmpool +10 success, pending count down ~40% on canary nodes. Continuing to monitor.
Nate: Great — keep an eye on preemptions and cross-AZ spill. If all good in 1h we can bake change into affinity rollout and close ticket.
Clara: Closing loop when stable.
